data.summary: Simplest setup for RyukLabs, hosted in the EU (Frankfurt, QE5069FF9): five managed services, nothing to operate. Vercel Pro runs the three Next.js apps (web app, engine API, operator console), the scheduled jobs and the secrets; Supabase holds Postgres (row-level security per tenant) and private file storage; Resend sends email; Firebase Cloud Messaging sends push to iOS and Android; Sentry reports errors and alerts to Slack. Staging and production are separate Vercel projects and separate Supabase projects, each tied to one Interlace environment (Q71D68AC5); pull-request previews are UI-only against the staging engine (Q7327AB74).

nodes.title: Engine API
nodes.about: The one backend: user endpoints under /api/v1, operator endpoints under /api/admin, the Interlace and email webhooks under /api/webhooks. It sets app.tenant_id per transaction and is the only client of Postgres.

nodes.title: Operator console
nodes.sub: Next.js, for Veil and tenant staff

nodes.title: Cron jobs
nodes.about: Vercel Cron calls each job on the engine with the cron secret; each job takes its lock in job_runs and records the outcome.

nodes.title: Postgres
nodes.about: Every table in the schema, with the engine's roles and grants; the Data API (PostgREST) is turned off.

nodes.title: Interlace
nodes.about: Card issuing, KYC review, wallets and Infinity Accounts; a sandbox for staging and production for live.

paths.name: A user signs in and is verified

steps.says: The app asks for a sign-in code, bound to this device
A six-digit code goes out by email
Each identity image is sent on its own, under the 4.5 MB body limit
It passes straight to Interlace; only the file id is kept, then KYC is submitted
KYC.UPDATED arrives: the signature is checked, the event stored, then processed
users.kyc_status is set and a kyc_passed notice recorded
The user sees they are verified
CARD.3DS.OTP: the merchant asks for a code
The code is kept in threeds_otps
The user reads the code and completes the payment
Ledger journals, entries and fee events are posted
Vercel Cron runs the webhook-retry job with the cron secret
Unprocessed webhook events are re-dispatched with backoff
After ten failed attempts the unprocessed-webhook ops alert fires

crossing.rule: The engine is the only door to the data: PostgREST is off, every request sets app.tenant_id, and row-level security per tenant is the backstop.
Browser calls cross origins only to the engine: CORS allows the app's own origins, with a cookie session and a CSRF token.
Interlace webhooks reach one receiver per deployment: the signature is checked with Veil's per-environment secret, the event stored and acknowledged within five seconds, then processed.
Money and card calls carry an Idempotency-Key and Veil's credentials, with the tenant's master merchant or the user's sub-merchant account.
Card numbers never touch SarusPay: a five-minute, single-use token opens Interlace's Widget.js frame in the app.
KYC images are never stored: each passes straight through the engine to Interlace and only its file id is kept.
Moving money, revealing a card, the PIN and devices need a trusted device; operators sign in with a password and an authenticator code.
A tenant goes live, or is suspended, only when a second platform owner approves the first one's request.

flows.title: A user action
steps: The web browser loads pages from the web app (app.saruspay.com) and calls the engine API on the tenant's API subdomain (api.saruspay.com) directly over HTTPS — CORS allows only app.saruspay.com and app-staging.saruspay.com (Q53F28838), with a cookie session and CSRF token; the mobile app calls the engine API with its session token; the console calls the engine server-side.
The engine authorises the session, sets app.tenant_id for the transaction and reads or writes Supabase Postgres (RLS is the backstop).
Money or card actions call Interlace with Veil's credentials and the tenant's master merchant or the user's sub-merchant accountId, with an Idempotency-Key.
The response returns to the client; events are recorded for notifications.

flows.title: An Interlace event
steps: Interlace posts to POST /api/webhooks/interlace on the engine.
The engine verifies the signature with Veil's per-environment webhook secret, stores the event and resolves tenant and user by accountId.
The handler applies effects (ledger, cards, deposits) and emits notifications; a failure leaves the event unprocessed.
The webhook-retry cron job re-runs unprocessed events with backoff; repeated failures raise an ops alert.

flows.title: Scheduled work
steps: Vercel Cron calls GET /api/admin/jobs/{name}/run with the cron secret on each job's schedule — every 5 minutes, every 15 minutes, hourly or daily (see Build → Jobs for the list). Cron runs on production deployments, so staging is its own Vercel project whose production branch runs staging cron.
Each job takes its lock in job_runs, does its work (fee-collection retry, reminders, ledger reconciliation, ops alerts, retention purge) and records the outcome.

flows.title: Email and push
steps: The engine sends email through Resend from the tenant's verified sender domain, or Veil's default sender until it verifies.
Push goes to Firebase Cloud Messaging, which delivers to Android directly and to iOS through Apple's push service.
Resend bounce events come back to POST /api/webhooks/email-provider.

flows.title: Files
steps: KYC images and ticket attachments upload to private Supabase Storage buckets through short-lived signed URLs.
The engine forwards KYC files to Interlace and serves attachments only through signed URLs to authorised operators.

flows.title: Build and release
steps: A pull request on GitHub deploys UI-only previews of the web app and console against the staging engine (engine previews are disabled).
Merging to main deploys the staging projects (engine, web app, console) against Interlace sandbox; merging main to release deploys the production projects.
Database changes run as Supabase migrations generated from tech/schema.sql, staging first; mobile builds go to TestFlight and Play internal testing before store release.

flows.title: A tenant goes live
steps: In staging, tenants are created live for testing. In production, a platform owner creates the tenant (state onboarding).

The onboarding checklist is completed (11 steps; sender domain verified is ticked automatically), the tenant's Interlace master merchant accountId is entered, a signed production webhook is received, and the tenant's production Firebase service account is set.

A platform owner requests go-live and a different platform owner approves (POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/go-live-requests). Suspending or reinstating a live tenant uses the same dual control (POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/suspension-requests).

environments.production: Production distributor account; tenants go live through the production-only go-live gate (Q71D68AC5)
